newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks smash more records as techs sizzle.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks smash more records as techs sizzle.

text.p: U.S. stocks shattered more records on Wall Street as technology stocks stormed higher on hopes that the cyclical downturn in chips had bottomed after reports of encouraging comments from Applied Materials.

"Techs are on fire. It's a flight to earnings growth. Investors in the slow growth economic environment are clearly favoring the large-cap blue chip technology names that will produce solid double-digit earnings increases over the couple of years," said Philip Orlando of Value Line Asset Management.
The Dow industrials surged 53 or 0.83 percent to about 6472.
The New York Stock Exchange imposed curbs on certain program trading at 1555 EST/2055 GMT.
It was the Dow's 42nd record closing high for 1996 and the 11th for November.
The S&P 500 climbed six to about 749, topping the previous record of 743.95 set Wednesday. The NYSE Composite rose two to about 395, also surpassing Wednesday's record of 392.80.
The tech-studded Nasdaq Composite soared 16 points or 1.28 percent to an unofficial record of 1274. The previous all-time high close of 1270.36 was set November 14.
Bellwether IBM surged 4-3/4 to 158-5/8.

While IBM has skyrocketed more than 70 percent from its July low of 90-1/4, Ken Tower, a technical analyst at UST Securities said further gains may be seen and that the overall market appeared healthy technically.

Despite the recent explosive upward move in equities, Tower said a study conducted by UST showed a majority has underperformed the S&P 500's 18 percent gain. "Out of the 6,000 stocks we follow, 69 percent have underperformed since the July bottom and 32 percent are lower than the July bottom. ... It's a broad rally but not a barn-burner or a speculative rally from the traditional standpoint," Tower said.

One laggard group that rallied on Friday was the semiconductor equipment sector. Industry flagship Applied Materials said that even at the low point in the current cycle, it expects profit margins to remain higher than in previous market cycles, analysts said.

Applied Materials rallied 6-5/8 to 38-5/8 as several brokers raised ratings. KLA Instruments climbed 5-1/4 to 38-1/2, Tencor was up 5-3/4 to 27, Lam Research rose 4-9/16 to 34-1/16, Novellus jumped 9-49/64 to 59-3/4 and PRI Automation was up 6-5/8 to 43-1/8. Microprocessor giant Intel, the most likely beneficiary of a recovery, was up 3-5/8 to 122-1/2.

Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage, noted that this is traditionally a strong time of the year for the stock market, "so it would be pretty surprising to see any type of tumble here. We have lot of momentum and people are hanging onto the stocks they want. It's a supply/demand question."
Several IPOs attracted strong interest. Nu Skin Asia Pacific, the exclusive Asian distributor of Nu Skin International personal products, surged 5-3/4 to 28-3/4.
CANTV, the Venezuelan telephone company, climbed 2-7/8 to 25-7/8 in its first day of trading. Rogue Wave Software shares jumped to 14-3/4 from their IPO price of 12.

Among individual shares, custom chip maker VLSI Technology lost 2-3/8 to 22-5/8. It plans to stop production at its San Jose wafer fabrication plant by the end of 1997, a move that will result in 300 job cuts and a fourth-quarter charge of $100-120 million.
Alrenco, an operator of rental-purchase stores, slumped 7-3/4 to 11-3/4 after warning of a fourth-quarter earnings shortfall.
Westell Technology, which forecast unexpectedly lower quarterly revenues, shed 4-5/16 to 23-11/16. Cowen downgraded Westell.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 16.28 to 1274.36, a record.
The S&P 500 index rose 5.98 to 748.73, a record.
For the week, the Dow rose 123.73 points.
Winners beat losers 1497 to 956 on very heavy NYSE volume of 525.2 million shares.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721.
